claim_one_line: WHERE A HIGGS CAN COUPLE THE ZERO MODES (sealed 6d6f7f660; PROVED -- every cell holds as sealed): no flat or harmonic Higgs couples the fibre's zero modes in the bulk (every non-zero pairing carries a non-trivial 2-torsion character, U2 to 5e-30); the pairing triplet v(z) = c_r th_r(0) th_r(z)/th_1(z) is isotropic at EVERY point (a theta identity, U3a to 7e-31), so at one tau a Higgs at any single point leaves one generation massless -- B1649's zero is a property of a single point, not of the puncture; the moves carry the triplet exactly at every point (U4: L, tau -> tau + 1, as Ad(g_L)^-1 and R, tau -> tau/(tau + 1), as Ad(g_R), with no Klein element, to 2e-16 at all four fixed points; a swapped-matrix control fails, 0.9976), and only the half-periods' triplets (0, -1, i), (i, 0, 1), (i, -1, 0) are independent of tau (U3b, with the puncture and generic points as controls); the lifts generate O, irreducible on M, and modulo the Klein group only the four real body diagonals are covariant (U5), so a covariant constant Higgs direction gives no hierarchy (B1646). Step 4 answered: under premise P1 (an even, single-point Higgs; tested by no cell) the covariant loci among the fixed points are the puncture, the half-period orbit, or both (surface frame), any of them at one tau -- the puncture is not forced, and P-129's first premise is a choice. Owed: the half-period orbit's mass structure (tau-independent triplets; to the frame tribunal, P-136), the legality of half-period fields (W60, P-108), the parabolic bulk statement, the odd Higgs's pair couplings. Corrected twice before the seal, both disclosed.
